title: Observe bounded file I/O
goal: Observe a small regular-file write/read while preserving a generous space reserve.
challenge: Use a fresh private workspace; check at least 528 MiB available. Write/read no more than one 16 MiB scratch file with the documented timers and child file-size limit. Retain timings and byte count, explain cache/virtual-disk limitations, then remove only that scratch file.

steps.explanation: Create a unique private guest workspace. Retain its printed path; repeat starts a new workspace, never overwrites old evidence. Stop if creation/change-directory fails.
steps.expected: A new /home/learner/capacity-io.XXXXXX directory. All files below are guest-local.

steps.explanation: Check the guest filesystem, not a raw device. Admission requires 540672 KiB: 512 MiB reserve plus 16 MiB payload. Stop if unavailable.
steps.expected: Normally much more is free; this check is not an aggregate quota or permanent reservation.

steps.command: test "$PWD" = "$work" && available=$(df -Pk . | awk 'NR==2 {print $4}') && [ "$available" -ge 540672 ] && TIMEFORMAT='%3R seconds' && { time ( ulimit -f 16384; timeout -k 2s 15s dd if=/dev/zero of=io.bin bs=1M count=16 conv=fsync status=none ); } 2> write-time.txt
steps.explanation: Read the whole line first. Guard the directory/reserve; the subshell limits each output file to 16 MiB (Bash’s default 1024-byte ulimit units). dd writes only io.bin, never a device. Record any error instead of interpreting failed I/O as throughput.
steps.expected: On success io.bin is exactly 16777216 bytes. The fsync write may be cached/virtualized; timeout is 15 seconds plus 2-second kill grace.

steps.command: test "$PWD" = "$work" && TIMEFORMAT='%3R seconds' && { time timeout -k 2s 15s dd if=io.bin of=/dev/null bs=1M count=16 status=none; } 2> read-time.txt
steps.explanation: Read at most the same payload to /dev/null; this is not a physical-disk benchmark. No cache dropping or direct I/O.
steps.expected: A read can be extremely fast or slow; a faster read is consistent with cache, not proof of its sole cause.

steps.explanation: Keep byte count, completion/error and elapsed observations. Do not compute throughput from a rounded zero duration.
steps.expected: 16777216 bytes only if the write succeeded; inconclusive measurements are accepted.

steps.command: if [ "$PWD" = "$work" ]; then rm -f -- io.bin; fi; ls -l
steps.explanation: Remove only the named scratch file in the verified working directory; repeat safely. Keep small timing notes.
steps.expected: io.bin is gone; evidence files remain. No recursive cleanup or broad termination.

hints: 528 MiB is 540672 KiB; the reserve is 512 MiB after a 16 MiB payload.
A timer/error or size mismatch invalidates a speed claim; retain it as failed/inconclusive evidence.
Page cache and host storage make these observations unsuitable for buying hardware based on one run.
review: I checked reserve, directory and exact scratch bytes.
I recorded successful or inconclusive timings without fixed thresholds.
I removed only io.bin and retained small notes.
coverage: Partial 200.1 file-I/O observations; no device attribution, iostat/sar or hardware benchmark. Completion records self-review, not verified guest assessment; there is no score.
